info.title: Wallow API
info.description: A modular monolith API built with Clean Architecture, DDD, and CQRS

post.summary: Create a new API key for the current user.
post.description:
Creates an API key that can be used for service-to-service authentication.
The full API key is only returned once in this response - store it securely!

The key will be scoped to the current user's tenant.

Example request:
```json
{
  "name": "Production Backend",
  "scopes": ["storage.read", "storage.write"],
  "expiresAt": "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

get.summary: List all API keys for the current user.
get.description:
Returns metadata for all API keys belonging to the authenticated user.
The actual key values are not returned - only the prefix for identification.

delete.description:
Permanently revokes an API key. This action cannot be undone.
Any requests using this key will be rejected immediately.

get.summary: The client's branding as its organization sees it.

put.summary:
Replace the client's branding: display name, tagline, optional logo upload and the curated
theme (`primary` and `primaryForeground` per `light`/`dark` mode). The
display name may never read as the platform itself.

delete.summary: Remove the client's logo. The rest of the branding stays.

post.summary:
Joins the caller to the inviting organization. Refused unless the caller's own verified
email is the one the invitation names, so a forwarded token grants nothing.

get.summary: The applications the caller has consented to.
get.description:
One entry per durable consent record, naming the client and the scopes the caller agreed
to. First-party sign-ins never appear here — their authorizations are session bookkeeping,
not consent.

delete.summary: Withdraws one consent, revoking the authorization and every token issued under it.
delete.description:
Refresh tokens chained to the authorization fail with `invalid_grant`, and issued
access tokens are refused on their next request. Answers 404 for an authorization that
does not exist or is not the caller's own.

get.summary: The organizations the caller belongs to.
get.description:
This is the organization picker's data: a first-party app lists these and re-authorizes
with the `organization` hint to switch context. The token it holds still opens one
organization's door at a time, so the switch is a new authorize round-trip, never a
header. Reachable without an organization, because a caller who belongs to three and
has picked none must be able to see them.

Asks for no permission — the answer is about the caller, and demanding one would hide
every organization but the one their token is scoped to, which is the question.

post.summary:
Issues a short-lived enrollment token for a fully-authenticated user.
The Web app calls this (with a bearer token) to get a token it can pass to the
Auth app's /mfa/enroll page, which exchanges it for an Identity.MfaPartial cookie
so the enrollment API calls can authenticate the user.

Exchanges a short-lived enrollment token for an Identity.MfaPartial cookie.
Called during Auth app prerender so the CookieForwardingHandler relays the
partial cookie to the browser, enabling subsequent enrollment API calls.

Register a developer application or a service account for the organization. The response
carries the client secret exactly once. A service account ignores every URI field.

get.summary: List the clients the organization owns.

post.summary:
Replace the client secret. The response carries the new secret exactly once; the old one
stops working immediately. `revokeActiveTokens` also ends every token the client was
already issued.

get.summary: Get one of the organization's clients.

patch.summary:
Replace a client's redirect URIs, logout URI and scopes. Name and client id are immutable;
a service account's URI fields are ignored.

delete.summary:
Delete one of the organization's clients for good: every credential it holds is revoked
first, then the client, its consents and its branding are removed.

post.summary:
Suspend a client: every token it was issued stops working now and its realtime connections
are closed, while its configuration, branding and consents are kept for reinstatement.
Reinstate a suspended client exactly as it was.

Place the platform's own suspension on the client, with a reason (global admins only).
While it stands the client is refused everywhere, whatever its own status says, and the
organization can read the reason but not lift it.

delete.summary:
Lift the platform suspension (global admins only). The client serves again unless the
organization's own suspension still stands.

post.summary: Create a new organization.
post.description:
Any account holder may found an organization without an operator, so this asks for no
permission and answers an organization-less token: a permission would have to be
granted by an organization the caller does not yet have.

get.summary: Get all organizations with optional search filtering and pagination.
Get a specific organization by ID.

delete.summary: Permanently delete an organization. Requires name confirmation.

get.summary: Get all members of a specific organization.

post.summary: Add a user to an organization.

delete.summary: Remove a user from an organization.

get.summary: List the organization's outstanding access requests, oldest first.
List the members whose access is currently taken away, most recently suspended first.

List the requests this organization turned away and has not taken back, most recently
refused first.

post.summary: Admit a pending requester, granting them the organization's default role.
Turn a pending requester away.

delete.summary: Let a denied requester ask again now, instead of waiting out the denial.

post.summary:
Take an active member's access to this organization away, keeping the membership so it can
be reinstated.
Give a suspended member their access back.
Give up your own membership of an organization.
post.description:
Asks for no permission and consults no access policy: the caller is deciding about
themselves, and requiring one would shut out members of every organization that is not the
one their token is scoped to — which is most of them. Membership itself is the authority
here, so a caller who has none gets the same refusal a stranger does.

post.summary: Archive an organization.
Reactivate an archived organization.

Place the platform's own suspension on the organization, with a reason (global admins
only). Every bound client's and every member's tokens are revoked, and every change to
the organization is refused while the suspension stands.

delete.summary:
Lift the organization's platform suspension (global admins only). Nothing is revoked
back into place: people sign in again, and clients the organization suspended itself
stay suspended.

get.summary: Get organization branding.

post.summary: Upload organization branding logo.

get.summary: Get organization settings.

put.summary: Set who may join this organization and the role they join with.
put.description:
Separate from the settings route above, and gated on managing members rather than on editing
settings: these three fields decide the organization's membership.

get.summary: Get all available roles in the system.
Get the permissions associated with a specific role.
List available API scopes with optional category filter.
Get a paginated list of users with optional search filtering.

post.summary: Create a new user account.

get.summary: Get a specific user by their ID.
Get the currently authenticated user's profile, roles, and permissions.

post.summary: Deactivate a user account.
Activate a previously deactivated user account.

Assign a role to a user IN THE CALLER'S OWN ORGANIZATION. The organization is the ambient
tenant rather than a parameter, so this route can never grant a role somewhere the caller
was not already authorized; the grant lands on the user's membership of that organization
and confers nothing in any other. The reserved global-administrator name is rejected:
global admin is a seeded claim, never a role, so it cannot be granted from inside a tenant.

delete.summary:
Remove a role from a user in the caller's own organization. Revocation is scoped the same
way the grant was, so it cannot reach a role the user holds elsewhere.

get.summary: Get the current user's notification history.
Get the current user's unread notification count.

post.summary: Mark a single notification as read.
Mark all notifications as read for the current user.
Create a new storage bucket.

get.summary: Get bucket by name.

post.summary: Upload a file.

get.summary: Get file metadata by ID.
Download a file (redirects to presigned URL).
List files in a bucket.

post.summary: Get a presigned URL for direct upload to storage.

Complete a presigned upload: verify the object exists, scan it, and promote the file
to Available (or Rejected). Idempotent once the file has left PendingValidation.

get.summary: Get a presigned URL for downloading a file.

AccountLoginResponse.description:
Result of a cookie-based sign-in attempt. A 200 covers four outcomes — signed in, MFA
challenge required, MFA enrollment required, and MFA enrollment required within a grace
period — so every member beyond bool AccountLoginResponse.Succeeded is present only for the outcome it
describes.

AccountOperationResponse.description:
Success envelope returned by the cookie-auth account endpoints that report only whether the
operation was carried out (registration, password reset, e-mail verification, magic link and
OTP dispatch).

AddMemberRequest.description:
Role is the name of the role this organization grants the member ("admin", "manager",
"user"). It is required: roles are per (user, organization), so there is no default to fall
back on.

ApiKeyCreatedResponse.description: Response when creating a new API key (includes the full key).

ClientTenantResponse.description:
The tenant an OIDC client belongs to, used by the auth frontend to brand the login screen
before any user is authenticated.

ConnectedApplicationDto.description:
An application the user has granted durable consent to: one Valid permanent authorization,
named by the client it authorizes and the scopes the user agreed to.

CreateAdminRequest.description:
First-run wizard input. The organization is part of it because roles are granted per
organization: without one the new administrator would hold no permission anywhere.

CreateApiKeyRequest.description: Request to create a new API key.

CreateClientRequest.description:
Scopes is what the client may ever request at the authorize endpoint. Omitting it grants the
OIDC sign-in baseline; API scopes are opt-in. FrontchannelLogoutUri is the absolute http(s)
address the logout page notifies (in a hidden iframe, with iss + sid) when the SSO session
ends; omitting it opts the client out of logout notifications.

isGlobalAdmin.description:
Whether the caller holds the platform operator's own authority — minted as its own
claim at sign-in, never derived from organization roles. The web app renders the
platform-suspension controls only for callers carrying it.

EnrollmentPolicy.description:
How an organization admits someone who is not already a member. Invitation acceptance is not
governed by this — being invited by a member holding `OrganizationsManageMembers` is itself
the authorization.

MfaBackupCodesResponse.description:
Regenerated one-time backup codes. The plaintext codes are returned here and nowhere else —
only their hashes are persisted.

MfaChallengeResponse.description:
Result of answering an MFA challenge, carrying the single-use ticket the auth frontend
exchanges for a sign-in cookie.

MfaEnrollmentConfirmedResponse.description:
Confirmation that TOTP enrollment completed, carrying the one-time backup codes. The plaintext
codes are returned here and nowhere else — only their hashes are persisted.

MfaEnrollmentSecretResponse.description: A freshly generated TOTP secret plus the otpauth URI an authenticator app scans.

MfaEnrollmentTokenResponse.description:
A short-lived token the web app hands to the auth app's enrollment screen, which exchanges it
for the partial-auth cookie the enrollment endpoints authenticate against.

MfaOperationResponse.description: Success envelope for the MFA endpoints that report only whether the operation was carried out.

MfaStatusResponse.description: The signed-in user's current multi-factor enrollment state.

MyOrganizationDto.description:
One organization the caller may sign in to. A client is bound to a single organization, so
an app can only ever link to the others — the slug is what it links with, and the name is
what it shows.

OrganizationClientRegistrationResponse.description:
The one-time reveal a registration or a secret rotation answers with: the client secret is
returned here and never again, and the issuer and API base URL are what the client's
environment must point at.

platformSuspendedAt.description: When the platform operator suspended this client, or `null`.

platformSuspensionReason.description: The operator's reason, readable by the organization's admins but not liftable by them.

OrganizationDto.description:
The platform-suspension pair is present so the owning organization's admins can read the
operator's reason; only a global admin can place or lift the suspension itself.

OrganizationLogoResponse.description: Location of an organization branding logo after upload.

PasswordlessVerificationResponse.description:
Result of verifying a magic link or one-time code, carrying the single-use ticket the auth
frontend exchanges for a sign-in cookie.

PlatformSuspensionRequest.description:
Places a platform suspension. The reason is the operator's and travels with the suspension:
the affected organization's admins read it, only a global admin removes it. The length cap
matches the column both suspension marks persist the reason into.

RedirectUriValidationResponse.description: Whether a candidate post-login redirect URI is registered for the requesting client.

RegisterOrganizationClientBranding.description:
Optional initial branding for an application: the end-user-facing display name (defaults to
the client's name) and a tagline. Ignored for service accounts, which face no end user.

RegisterOrganizationClientRequest.description:
Registers a client on behalf of an organization. `Kind` is `application` for a
developer application a person signs in to or `service-account` for a client-credentials
client. Name and the derived client id are immutable once registered. An application needs at
least one redirect URI, absolute, fragment-free, and https or http://localhost; a service
account ignores every URI field. Both need at least one scope.

RoleResponse.description: A role available for assignment within the tenant.

RotateOrganizationClientSecretRequest.description:
Rotates a client's secret. `RevokeActiveTokens` additionally ends every token the client
was already issued, so a compromise response cuts every live session in the same step.

SetupStatusResponse.description:
Whether first-run setup is still open and, while it is, the organization the bootstrap
administrator will own. OrganizationName is the one organization the seed
already created (the one the dashboard client is bound to) so the setup page can offer it
rather than let the visitor type a name that creates a sibling; `null` when
setup is complete or when there is not exactly one organization to offer.

UpdateClientRequest.description:
A full replacement of the client's mutable registration — omitting FrontchannelLogoutUri
un-registers the client from front-channel logout notifications, matching how the URI lists
replace rather than merge.

UpdateOrganizationClientRequest.description:
Everything about a client its organization may change after registration. Name and client id
are immutable and deliberately absent.

UpdateOrganizationEnrollmentRequest.description:
Who may join an organization and on what terms. Separate from
UpdateOrganizationSettingsRequest because these fields are gated on the right to
manage members, not the right to edit settings.
